tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session logs show: navigation to an admin order view, a login step (handled before tool execution), clicking Reorder which navigates to sales_order_create, then clicking the final Submit Order button (scoped selector) to create a new admin order. The session confirms the reorder flow succeeds and results in an admin order view page with a success message and new order id.

Task Definition:
- Build a deterministic, re-usable tool that: given the admin base URL and a source order_id, navigates to that order, triggers the Reorder action, submits the resulting New Order form, and verifies creation of the new order.

Action Plan (detailed):
1) Navigate to the specific order view URL to ensure the correct order context.
2) Trigger Reorder by navigating directly to the conventional reorder URL (/sales_order/reorder/order_id/{id}/) — this is deterministic and avoids fragile text-only selectors.
3) Wait for the sales_order_create (New Order) page to load and extract a snapshot of items and totals for verification.
4) Click the final Submit Order button using a scoped XPath that selects the last 'Submit Order' control on the page (the one near Order Totals).
5) Wait for navigation/response and extract post-submit content: success message, order header and URL to confirm creation.

Variable Identification:
- base_admin_url (string, required): the admin base URL including admin frontName (used to construct order and reorder URLs).
- order_id (string, required): internal numeric order_id to reorder from; inserted into URLs.
- timeout_seconds (number, optional): to control waits/timeouts (default used if omitted).

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- The original UI flow clicked visible Reorder and Submit buttons. Because Magento uses predictable admin URLs for reorder (sales_order/reorder/order_id/<id>) and the reorder step typically triggers a GET that opens sales_order_create, we replace the UI 'click' for Reorder with a direct navigation to the constructed reorder URL. This increases reliability and avoids localization issues. For the Submit Order action we must click a button; multiple 'Submit Order' instances exist on the page so we use an XPath that picks the last occurrence (scoped to Order Totals with alternative XPaths provided in the analysis).
- Navigation steps are deterministic and avoid ambiguous selectors. The Submit click uses a stable XPath that uses position (last()) to avoid clicking the header duplicate. Post-submit verification relies on standard Magento indicators: admin success flash message and redirect to /sales_order/view/.

Assumptions and Caveats:
- The automation environment is already authenticated into the admin session. The tool will not perform login.
- The admin frontName and base URL must be accurate; if the site uses custom admin routing other than the provided base, the constructed URLs will need to be adjusted.
- Some Magento installs may require a form_key parameter for certain actions; in many admin setups sales_order/reorder/order_id/{id}/ works for logged-in admin users. If the environment requires additional tokens, a DOM-based click (extract href from the live DOM and navigate to it) or including form_key may be necessary—this tool uses the conventional URL approach which matched the recorded session.
- The Submit Order click is performed by XPath selector which assumes the final submit is a <button> or input rendered as last submit control. If the admin theme uses different markup, replace the XPath with a site-specific selector.

The tool steps are minimal and essential: 1) confirm order view, 2) perform reorder via URL, 3) snapshot new order, 4) click final Submit Order, 5) confirm order creation. No optional exploratory steps are included.
name: magento_admin_reorder_create_order
description: Navigate to a Magento 1.x admin order, perform the Reorder action for a given order_id, then submit the resulting admin New Order (sales_order_create) form and verify the order was created. Uses direct URL navigation for reliability and scoped XPath to click the final Submit Order button.

steps.description: Open the admin Order View page for the provided order_id to ensure we're on the correct order before performing Reorder.
Allow the Order View page to finish loading (small pause to let JS render topbar actions).

Perform the Reorder action by navigating directly to the conventional admin reorder URL (avoids brittle text-only button selection). This opens the New Order (sales_order_create) page pre-filled from the original order.
Wait for the New Order page (sales_order_create) to load and for the cart/items to be pre-filled.
Extract Items list, subtotal, shipping, tax and grand total and basic account info. This is used to assert expected content prior to final submit.
steps.goal: Capture a snapshot of the New Order page to verify items, totals and customer context before submitting

steps.description: Click the scoped final 'Submit Order' control (selects the last matching Submit Order button on the page — the one in the Order Totals area).
steps.xpath: (//button[normalize-space(text())='Submit Order' or normalize-space(@title)='Submit Order' or normalize-space(@value)='Submit Order'])[last()]

steps.description: Wait for the submit action to complete and the admin to redirect to the Order View or show a success message.
Extract success messages and page header to confirm a new order was created, and capture the new order identifier shown on the page.
steps.goal: Verify order creation: detect admin success flash message, capture resulting order view header (Order #...), and check the current URL contains '/sales_order/view/'

input_schema.name: base_admin_url
input_schema.description: Full Magento admin base URL up to the admin frontName (include protocol). Example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin"

input_schema.name: order_id
input_schema.description: Numeric internal order_id used in admin URLs (e.g. "204"). This is the source order to reorder from and will be inserted into admin URLs.

input_schema.name: timeout_seconds
input_schema.description: Maximum seconds to wait for each navigation or post-click confirmation. Defaults to 30 if omitted.
